title: Invertibility of finite and sequence coefficient inverse image
statement: Let ell be prime, E a finite extension of Q_ell and f:X→Y any scheme map. Let s select a positive finite coefficient exponent or the whole ringed sequence site, with coefficients, ringPush, ringPull and ringMap as constructed in [lem-sf-ambient-pullback-site-constructions]. The adjunct ringMap(f,s):ringPull(f,s)(coefficients(Y,s))→coefficients(X,s) is an isomorphism. No flatness or cartesian condition is assumed on horizontal module transitions.

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03EL; sites.tex 03CB; sites-cohomology.tex 06YN, 06YS, 07A4, 0G7E and 0G7D. Specialized construction and proof from the ambient coherence argument.

proof.text: At finite level both inverse-image-of-constant-sheaf and constant sheaf are left adjoints to evaluation of direct image at the terminal object. Base change preserves that terminal object, so their right adjoints agree canonically. The unique left-adjoint comparison is an isomorphism, and the constant-section unit equation identifies it with ringMap.

On the product sequence site, a sheaf of rings is its sequence of vertical ring sheaves and horizontal ring homomorphisms. Form the inverse image in each vertical fiber. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction bijections restricts them to families commuting with every horizontal map; this is the adjunction to product base-change direct image. Thus the finite coefficient isomorphisms give a morphism of the actual ring sequences. Its inverse family also commutes with transitions by conjugating each transition square. These are mutually inverse on every section, which proves invertibility on the whole ringed site.

proof_origin.place: Explicit specialization and glue for the cited adjunction, tensor and K-flat arguments; no change to the unit route.
